children: Analytics and artificial-intelligence software firm Databricks plans to invest more than $350 million in Singapore over the next three years to tap growing demand for its business in Asia.
Simon Davies, general manager for Asia-Pacific and Japan at the San Francisco-based company, said Wednesday that Databricks' business in the region more than doubled in the second quarter.
Databricks was valued at $190 billion after a fundraising round in August.
The company also said it plans to double its headcount in Singapore to over 500.
"Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing [region] and the plan is for us to continue to be the fastest-growing in the years to come," Davies said.
Over 20,000 organizations use Databricks' AI platform, including Block, Comcast, Condé Nast, Rivian and Shell, according to its website.
